A Little About Me

One Guy. 18 Years. I Still Pick Up the Phone.

I started doing handyman work in 2006 after spending years in construction. I wanted to do smaller jobs — the kind that matter to homeowners but aren't worth calling a big contractor for. Turns out, there's a lot of that work out there.

When you hire me, you get me. Not a crew I dispatched, not a sub I've never met — me. I'll look at your project, tell you what I think it'll take, and give you a price before I start. If something changes mid-job, I call you. No surprises on the invoice.

  • 18 years of hands-on experience — residential repairs, not just new builds
  • Fully insured — happy to provide proof before any job
  • I work Monday through Saturday, no weekend surcharge
  • I don't take on jobs I can't do right — I'll tell you if something needs a specialist

FAQ

Questions I Get a Lot

Do you charge by the hour or by the job?

Both, depending on the work. Small repairs are usually by the job — you get a flat price upfront. Longer or less predictable projects (like a full deck repair where I won't know the extent until I start) are hourly. I'll tell you which applies before I start, always.

How far in advance do I need to book?

Usually 3–5 days for non-urgent jobs. If something's an emergency — a broken door that won't lock, a leak — call me and I'll do my best to get there sooner. I work Monday through Saturday so there's usually flexibility.

Are you licensed and insured?

Yes. I carry general liability insurance and maintain my handyman registration. I'll provide proof before any job if you need it — most people ask, and I understand why.

Do you do electrical or HVAC work?

Light fixtures, ceiling fans, outlet covers, switches — yes. Full rewiring or panel work — no, that needs a licensed electrician and I'll tell you so. Same with HVAC: filter swaps and basic stuff yes, compressor work no. I won't take a job I can't do right.

What if the job turns out to be bigger than expected?

I call you before I go further. You decide whether to proceed, adjust scope, or stop — no surprise charges on your invoice. I'd rather have that conversation than have you unhappy at the end.
